text: Icon (Arnus; alias Augustus Freeman) is a fictional superhero published by DC Comics, one of the original characters introduced by Milestone Media in the 1990s. A being from another planet, he has taken on the form of an African-American man and possesses abilities such as flight, super-strength, and invulnerability. He partners with Rocket, a human teenager using alien technology, to protect the people of Dakota City. Created by Dwayne McDuffie and M. D. Bright, Icon first appeared in Icon #1 (May 1993) and was part of a separate continuity from the main DC Universe, despite being published and distributed by DC Comics. The character appeared monthly in his own series until the Milestone imprint ended in 1997. In 1994, he participated in Worlds Collide, a month-long crossover between Milestone and DC's Superman titles. In the late 2000s, the Milestone Universe was revived and merged into the DC Universe as part of a deal between DC Comics and Milestone Media, with the characters treated as new to the universe and the prior crossover ignored. Icon, along with Shadow Cabinet, appeared in Justice League of America (vol. 2) #27, written by McDuffie. In 1839, an alien starliner malfunctioned and exploded, jettisoning a life-pod in a cotton field in the American South. The pod automatically altered the appearance of its passenger, Arnus, to mimic an enslaved black woman named Miriam, who witnessed the pod land and adopted Arnus as her son. Arnus has longevity that makes him appear middle-aged despite being centuries old, and as a result, he periodically assumes the identity of his own son. By the late 20th century, he is posing as Augustus Freeman IV, the great-grandson of his original human identity, and becomes a superhero alongside his protégé Rocket. Icon's lifepod altered his DNA to resemble a human, enabling him to blend into Earth's population, and this process maximized his hybrid genetic structure, granting him superhuman abilities such as immense strength, durability, speed, senses, and the ability to project radiant energy, including low-energy bolts that can render humans unconscious and overload electronic devices. Icon ages at a much slower rate than humans, making him appear middle-aged despite being several centuries old, and his lifespan is typical for a Terminan, with only the genetic maximization providing his powers. Icon is an experienced lawyer with decades of experience and a formidable combatant whose fighting skills are close to those of Superman, having fought in major conflicts from the Civil War to World War II. For interstellar travel, Icon uses his personal starship, which has a faster-than-light drive that allows it to enter hyperspace, and gravity compensators that provide adjustable artificial gravity. The ship is linked to the Info Tool, a computerized database that scans and stores the molecular structure of any item (organic or inorganic) in files called "software," and can link to and control any computer-operated device or system. The Maker is a molecular factory that constructs physical items molecule by molecule from structural data files stored in the Info Tool, with these files called "software" and the resulting objects called "hardware." The ship also has cloaking technology that renders it invisible to both the human eye and electronic surveillance, a feature installed specifically so Icon could operate undetected on Earth. Icon appears in Young Justice, voiced by Tony Todd, where he is an associate and later member of the Justice League. Icon is a conservative Republican with conservative views on economic and social issues, often clashing with more liberal Milestone superheroes, including Rocket. Supreme Court Justice Clarence Thomas was a known fan of Icon, quoting the character multiple times, which caused author Dwayne McDuffie, who described himself as liberal, to experience writer's block due to concerns that his dialogue would be used to promote conservatism. Icon was nominated for three Eisner Awards and has won three Parents' Choice Awards. ISBN 1-4012-2549-7 (Reprint: October 6, 2009). During the Final Crisis event, Orion kills Darkseid, destabilizing the space-time continuum and threatening both the Dakotaverse and the mainstream DC universe. Dharma uses energies from the entity Rift to merge the two universes, creating a new continuity and altering history so that the residents of the Dakotaverse have always existed in the DC universe. Only Dharma, Icon, and Superman are aware that Dakota and its inhabitants ever existed in a parallel universe.
